# Design records

Each decision about how OML works is a numbered record in the repository, with the alternatives it rejected. The records are not part of this site. This page lists all 59 by subject, and each row links to the record on GitHub.

*Generated by `scripts/gen_design_records.py`; edit the source, not this page.*

## Storage and data

Where memory lives, how it is encrypted, drained to the lake and erased.

| Record | Status | Decision |
|---|---|---|
| [ADR-0002](https://github.com/e8kor/open-memory-lab/blob/main/docs/adr/ADR-0002-postgresql-system-of-record.md) | accepted design | PostgreSQL is the system of record: one commit point, per-tenant signed chains, a synchronous journal domain |
| [ADR-0003](https://github.com/e8kor/open-memory-lab/blob/main/docs/adr/ADR-0003-delta-lake-derived-lakehouse.md) | accepted design | Delta Lake is the derived body lakehouse: outbox-fed, single-writer, never the authority |
| [ADR-0004](https://github.com/e8kor/open-memory-lab/blob/main/docs/adr/ADR-0004-bodies-and-attachments.md) | accepted design | Bodies and attachments: content-addressed, per-artifact encryption, digest-only journal |
| [ADR-0005](https://github.com/e8kor/open-memory-lab/blob/main/docs/adr/ADR-0005-erasure-by-crypto-shredding.md) | accepted design | Erasure by crypto-shredding, with a named inventory and an honest boundary |
| [ADR-0017](https://github.com/e8kor/open-memory-lab/blob/main/docs/adr/ADR-0017-reconciliation.md) | accepted design | Reconciliation is an incremental, journalled fold with a closed finding vocabulary |
| [ADR-0060](https://github.com/e8kor/open-memory-lab/blob/main/docs/adr/ADR-0060-the-lake-writer-drains-the-outbox-it-has-seals-what-it-materializes-and-answers-only-the-operator.md) | accepted design | The lake writer drains the outbox it has, seals what it materializes, and answers only the operator |

## Search and recall

How recall finds, ranks and filters memories.

| Record | Status | Decision |
|---|---|---|
| [ADR-0013](https://github.com/e8kor/open-memory-lab/blob/main/docs/adr/ADR-0013-reads-served-from-postgres.md) | accepted design | Reads are served from Postgres, journalled: one serving tier, a logged read path, steering ahead of hits |
| [ADR-0048](https://github.com/e8kor/open-memory-lab/blob/main/docs/adr/ADR-0048-search-improves-in-stages-any-word-first-meaning-last-each-gated-on-the-recall-eval.md) | proposed | Search improves in stages: any word first, meaning last, each gated on the recall eval |
| [ADR-0049](https://github.com/e8kor/open-memory-lab/blob/main/docs/adr/ADR-0049-search-is-a-pipeline-of-retrievers-behind-a-port-chosen-by-name-and-gated-by-the-recall-eval.md) | proposed | Search is a pipeline of retrievers behind a port, chosen by name and gated by the recall eval |
| [ADR-0052](https://github.com/e8kor/open-memory-lab/blob/main/docs/adr/ADR-0052-text-search-reads-integer-postings-that-row-security-lets-an-index-serve.md) | accepted design | Text search reads integer postings, which row security lets an index serve, and says when it pruned a word or scanned |
| [ADR-0053](https://github.com/e8kor/open-memory-lab/blob/main/docs/adr/ADR-0053-reranking-is-a-local-cross-encoder-stage-after-fusion-off-by-default-until-it-fits-the-latency-budget.md) | accepted design | Reranking is a local cross-encoder stage after fusion, off by default until it fits the latency budget |
| [ADR-0054](https://github.com/e8kor/open-memory-lab/blob/main/docs/adr/ADR-0054-recall-is-measured-by-what-readers-do-next-and-only-other-readers-use-moves-a-rank-within-a-bound.md) | accepted in part | Recall is measured by what readers do next, and only other readers' use moves a rank, within a bound |
| [ADR-0059](https://github.com/e8kor/open-memory-lab/blob/main/docs/adr/ADR-0059-a-memory-states-when-it-is-true-recall-hides-what-has-ended-and-searches-the-dates-a-query-names-without-a-model.md) | accepted design | A memory states when it is true, recall hides what has ended, and recall searches the dates a query names without a model |

## Integrations and agents

The API, the MCP tools, the plugin and the hooks agents use.

| Record | Status | Decision |
|---|---|---|
| [ADR-0014](https://github.com/e8kor/open-memory-lab/blob/main/docs/adr/ADR-0014-http-api-and-mcp-facade.md) | accepted design | One versioned JSON HTTP API; MCP streamable HTTP as a stateless facade |
| [ADR-0022](https://github.com/e8kor/open-memory-lab/blob/main/docs/adr/ADR-0022-two-ring-api.md) | accepted design | The two-ring API: v1 memory provider, v2 memory lab |
| [ADR-0025](https://github.com/e8kor/open-memory-lab/blob/main/docs/adr/ADR-0025-the-agent-only-memory-surface.md) | accepted design | One key writes and recalls through grants, and an agent reads back, budgets, supersedes and retires its own memory only through admission |
| [ADR-0028](https://github.com/e8kor/open-memory-lab/blob/main/docs/adr/ADR-0028-agent-key-issuance.md) | accepted design | The CLI issues an agent's key in one call with its reader grant by default, and an admin skill runs it without the key value entering a transcript |
| [ADR-0029](https://github.com/e8kor/open-memory-lab/blob/main/docs/adr/ADR-0029-session-start-hook.md) | accepted design | The agent plugin starts every session from what OML holds for its key, through `oml hook session-start` |
| [ADR-0031](https://github.com/e8kor/open-memory-lab/blob/main/docs/adr/ADR-0031-oauth-connections-by-connect-code.md) | accepted design | Claude's hosted apps reach the agent plugin over OAuth, through a connection that a one-time connect code binds to one agent key |
| [ADR-0037](https://github.com/e8kor/open-memory-lab/blob/main/docs/adr/ADR-0037-a-guardrail-is-a-reviewed-rule-loaded-at-session-start-and-checked-at-the-tool-call.md) | accepted design | A guardrail is a claim of its own kind, ratified under its workarea's review policy, that the agent plugin loads at every session start within the scope an admin set on its key, and whose optional rule a local hook checks before each tool call |
| [ADR-0038](https://github.com/e8kor/open-memory-lab/blob/main/docs/adr/ADR-0038-the-agent-recalls-for-itself-and-a-failed-command-recalls-only-when-opted-in.md) | accepted design | The agent recalls for itself, and a failed command recalls only when the user opted in |
| [ADR-0039](https://github.com/e8kor/open-memory-lab/blob/main/docs/adr/ADR-0039-the-api-rewritten-for-v0-4-0.md) | accepted design | The API is rewritten for v0.4.0 while OML is pre-release: three task-shaped MCP tools, a contract that declares only what is served, one URL and one key to start, and nothing lost |
| [ADR-0040](https://github.com/e8kor/open-memory-lab/blob/main/docs/adr/ADR-0040-plugin-setup-in-claude-code.md) | accepted design | The plugin takes its server URL and its key through Claude Code's plugin configuration, keeps the key in the keychain, and falls back to `OML_URL` and `OML_API_KEY` only in its hooks |

| [ADR-0042](https://github.com/e8kor/open-memory-lab/blob/main/docs/adr/ADR-0042-every-request-logs-one-line-under-an-id-the-caller-may-name-and-metrics-stay-off-the-public-port.md) | accepted design | Every request logs one line under an id the caller may name, metrics stay off the public port, and trace export is opt-in |

| [ADR-0046](https://github.com/e8kor/open-memory-lab/blob/main/docs/adr/ADR-0046-the-lifecycle-claim-edges-and-the-brief-ship-in-v0-5-2-inside-user-roots-with-no-new-tool.md) | accepted design | The lifecycle, claim edges and the brief ship in v0.5.2 inside user roots, with no new tool |
| [ADR-0058](https://github.com/e8kor/open-memory-lab/blob/main/docs/adr/ADR-0058-a-public-server-runs-to-stated-slos-with-an-error-budget.md) | accepted | A public server runs to stated SLOs with an error budget |
